video.acting_natural.evidence: [Riley·claude] I'm judging only Riley (me). With the sound off, the shot shows a woman in modern clothes walking into a bath changing room full of women in linen wraps. She looks around, then walks toward the niches in the left wall. That matches the key beat: she gets it at a glance and heads for the niches. 0–2.25s (row 1 to the first cells of row 2): my back is to the camera as I walk into the hall. My weight shifts naturally, my arms swing, and the bread bag hangs at my left hip and moves with my stride. Nothing is stiff. 2.5–4.0s: I keep walking to the middle of the hall and stop, with a natural slowdown before the stop. 4.25–6.0s: I turn sideways and my profile is visible. My face points toward the right wall and the women there. I stand still for about 1.75s, which reads as looking and taking things in, not as a frozen pose. This is how I would behave right after walking into a strange room. 6.25–7.75s: I turn and walk across toward the left-hand row, moving like someone who has just figured it out and is heading over. 8.0–8.75s: I stop on the left side of the walkway, beside the seated women, facing the left wall. The cause and effect is clear: I look, I understand, I walk over to find a spot. My reactions come on time, I don't overdo anything, and I don't repeat a gesture. Two small notes: (1) I look right first and then go left, while the spec has me looking left first. That is a spec issue, not an acting one, and it doesn't change this verdict. (2) The cells are too small to make out my small smile and nod at 4.3–5.5s, or whether I look up at the niches at the end. Nothing exaggerated or done only because the plot needs it is visible.
